tasks.short: Diagnose and treat an unstable or emergency condition with other providers.

steps.what: List stored problems, medications and the latest result.
Examine the patient for this emergency condition.
Decide the diagnosis of this complex comorbid condition.
Treat the unstable emergency condition in the room.
Speak with the other health care provider about this condition.
Draft the consultation note from what she just said.

loop.input: the diagnosis and the treatment she stated in the room
loop.check: she checks that the draft states that diagnosis and that treatment, not only the patient id
loop.stop: one draft, then stop; if she rejects it she writes the note herself
loop.why_not_simpler: the findings are free text, so a fixed form cannot draft the note

steps.what: Check the draft states the diagnosis and the treatment.
File the confirmed consultation note on the patient record.

tasks.design: The patient record in {OTHER} lists problem name, medication name and the latest result only when those fields are already stored. A draft note is produced from what she says, she checks that it states the diagnosis and the treatment, and only that confirmed version is filed. The list does not diagnose, the draft does not treat, and nothing sends an alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: The exam and the treatment were spoken in the room, and the record did not offer problem, medication and result as fields she could trust without opening every screen.
tasks.enabler_now: Stored fields can be listed, and a single draft can be checked before it is filed. The exam, the diagnosis and the treatment are unchanged.
tasks.still_hard: An unstable patient is in the room. A listed result does not diagnose, and a draft does not treat or speak to the other provider.
tasks.human_edge: She examines, she names the diagnosis, she treats, and she decides what the other provider must hear.
tasks.altitude: She still examines, diagnoses, treats and speaks with the other provider. She stops hunting the chart when problem, medication and result are filled, and she stops retyping a note she has checked.

reach.task: Takes over the emergency when she hands the patient across.
reach.learn: Which findings the physician needs before that handover.

reach.task: Stays with the unstable patient after she leaves the room.
reach.learn: Which treatment she must say aloud before she goes.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber records the consultation, the clinician validates, and the note can go into HiX, Nedap ONS or Nexus. The page claims 15 to 20 minutes saved per consult and gives no method. This design does not use that minute claim.
Tandem's scribe and coding carry an MDR class IIa mark.

At Capio Ramsay Santé, 1,295 clinicians and 236,153 Tandem notes, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes, and median editing stayed 93 seconds. Three of seven authors work for the vendor. That is note time, not this whole emergency visit.
The health inspectorate says providers remain responsible for careful use of generative AI and names medication errors from a wrong registration. This design files only a note she has checked.
Decision software that needs a notified body is high-risk from 2 August 2028, and Annex III duties start 2 December 2027. Whether this draft is that software is not settled here.
Annex III covers emergency triage and eligibility for care. This design does not triage who is seen and does not decide eligibility.
The dossier is kept twenty years after the last change. The filed note sits in that dossier. This design adds no second archive.
A decision based solely on automated processing needs an Article 22 basis. This design does not diagnose or choose the treatment by automation.
Ambient recording can capture staff performance and needs Dutch works-council consent where a council exists. Other countries differ. The draft does not score her.
Model knowledge: listing stored rows and drafting one note are not a measured saving for this employer. The range is a scenario for this visit, not a published percentage.

assumptions: She starts when the patient is in front of her and stops when the confirmed note is on the record. She does not run the lab and she does not take the physician's exam. Every step is her time.

The list reads problem name, medication name, result name and result value already stored by an earlier clinician or the lab, outside this visit. A blank field is omitted. She examines without it, and that exam stays at full time. Capture of those rows is not counted as saved.

The draft uses the diagnosis and the treatment she stated in s3 and s4. It does not invent either. A rejected draft is not filed. She then writes the note herself, and that extra time is the upkeep below.
Filing is a separate step. It writes only consult-note-v1, the version she accepted in s7. A later change voids that acceptance and nothing files.
Upkeep is 0.5 hour per 100 hours of this task, for a wrong-patient result row and for a draft that omitted the treatment. The check in s7 is already in remaining time and is not deducted again.
No step alerts a colleague, sends the note out, or fills another sheet. Speaking to the other provider stays in the room.
unknowns: Whether this record stores problem name, medication name, result name and result value as fields.
Whether the draft tool is classed as a medical device in this clinic.
Whether a works council exists and whether it treats consultation recording as staff monitoring.
research_questions: Which of those four fields are present on a sample of emergency visits this month?
Who may accept the note, and what happens to a draft she rejects?

already_counted.description: Read the draft for a missing diagnosis or a missing treatment.

incremental.description: Correct a result row on the wrong patient, or rewrite a draft that omitted the treatment.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a visit where problem, medication and result are filled and she accepts the draft, she skips the chart hunt and the retype. On a blank record, a rejected draft, or an emergency that is all hands-on care, the saving is near zero. The exam, the diagnosis, the treatment and the talk with the other provider are not shortened. The figure is not the published note-time percentage applied to the whole visit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prescribe dosage, route and frequency from the patient's age and gender.

steps.what: Show age, sex and current medication for this patient.
Decide the dosages, route and frequency from age and gender.
Flag interactions and dose limits for those dosages.
Decide whether those dosages still stand after the flags.
Tell the patient the dosages, route and frequency.
Prescribe those medication dosages on the line she signs.

tasks.design: The patient record in {OTHER} shows age, sex and current medication when those fields are stored. A rule check then flags interactions, contraindications and dose limits for the dosages she has already named. She still decides, tells the patient and writes the prescription herself. The check does not prescribe, does not send the prescription, and does not alert the pharmacy.
tasks.previous_blocker: Age, sex and the current medication sat on different screens, and the interaction lookup was a search she repeated for every dosage.
tasks.enabler_now: Those stored fields can be shown, and a rule check can flag a dosage she has named. Choosing the dosage and signing it stay with her.
tasks.still_hard: Age and gender do not set the dosage on their own. She still has to see the patient and sign the line.
tasks.human_edge: She chooses the dosage from the person in front of her, and she signs. A flag is a warning, not a prescription.
tasks.altitude: She still chooses the dosage, tells the patient and signs. She stops hunting age, sex and the current medication when those fields are filled, and she stops searching the interaction text by hand.

reach.learn: Which interaction flag the pharmacist treats as a hard stop.

evidence.claim: The G-Standaard checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates. KNMP sets the content. The check does not choose the dosage.
The inspectorate names medication errors that come from a wrong registration and says the provider stays responsible. This design does not let the flag change the dosage.
The cited source is the medicines-law definition of a prescription. This design does not treat a flag as that prescription. She writes the line herself.
A decision based solely on automated processing needs an Article 22 basis. This design does not choose the dosage by automation.
Model knowledge: showing stored characteristics and flagging a named dosage are not a measured saving for this employer. The range is a scenario for this prescription, not a published percentage.

assumptions: She starts when she is ready to prescribe for this patient and stops when she has signed the line. She does not dispense. Every step is her time. The pharmacist's dispensing is outside this task.

The list reads age in years, sex, current medication name and current dose, stored by registration and by the prescriber of the earlier line, outside this task. A blank is omitted. She asks age and reads the boxes during the decision and the telling, which stay at full time. That earlier capture is not counted as saved.

The flag runs only after she has named the dosages in s2. It shows interactions, contraindications and dose limits. It does not write the prescription, send it, or alert the pharmacy. A missing current-medication list is shown as missing and does not clear the dosage.
She writes and signs the line herself in s6. There is no separate send step because nothing in this design transmits the prescription.
Upkeep is 0.3 hour per 100 hours of this task, for a flag that used a stale medication row. Reading the flags is s4 and is not deducted again.
unknowns: Whether age, sex, current medication name and current dose are stored as fields on this record.
Whether the clinic already shows interaction flags, or she still searches a book.
Which flags this clinic treats as a hard stop.
research_questions: On a sample of prescriptions, how often are age, sex and the current medication filled before she decides?
How often does she change the dosage after seeing a flag?

incremental.description: Correct a flag that used a stale current-medication row.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a prescription where age, sex and current medication are filled, she skips the screen hunt and the hand search for interactions. On a blank age, a missing medication list, or a dosage she changes after the flags, the saving is near zero. Choosing the dosage, telling the patient and signing are not shortened. The figure is not a published prescribing percentage.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Diagnose and treat chronic problems such as blood pressure or diabetes.

steps.what: Show stored blood pressure and glucose for these problems.
Ask how these chronic health problems have been since last time.
Examine this patient for high blood pressure or diabetes.
Decide how to treat these chronic health problems today.
Tell the patient the treatment for the diabetes or the pressure.
Draft the chronic visit note from the treatment she chose.

loop.input: the symptom account, the exam and the treatment she stated
loop.check: she checks that the draft cites the diabetes or blood pressure decision, not only the patient id
loop.stop: one draft, then stop; if she rejects it she writes the note herself
loop.why_not_simpler: what the patient reports is free text, so a fixed form cannot draft the note

steps.what: Check the draft cites the diabetes or blood pressure decision.
File the confirmed note on these chronic health problems.

tasks.design: The patient record in {OTHER} shows stored blood pressure and glucose only when reading type, value and date are already stored. A draft note is produced from what she asks, examines and decides. She checks that it cites the diabetes or blood pressure decision, and only that confirmed version is filed. The list does not alert, and it does not decide the treatment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Earlier readings were scattered, and the visit note was retyped from memory after the patient had gone.
tasks.enabler_now: Stored readings can be shown, and one draft can be checked before it is filed. Asking, examining and deciding stay in the room.
tasks.still_hard: A glucose list does not say how the patient is today. She still examines and chooses the treatment.
tasks.human_edge: She hears the interval history, examines, and decides whether the chronic problem needs a change.
tasks.altitude: She still asks, examines, decides and tells the patient. She stops tallying old readings when they are stored, and she stops retyping a note she has checked.

reach.task: Repeats the blood pressure between these visits.
reach.learn: Which reading she wants repeated before the next visit.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber records the consultation, the clinician validates, and the note can go into HiX, Nedap ONS or Nexus. The page claims 15 to 20 minutes saved per consult and gives no method. This design does not use that minute claim.
Tandem's scribe and coding carry an MDR class IIa mark.

At Capio Ramsay Santé, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes across 236,153 notes, and median editing stayed 93 seconds. Three of seven authors work for the vendor. That is note time, not this whole chronic visit.
The health inspectorate says providers remain responsible for careful use of generative AI and names medication errors from a wrong registration. This design files only a note she has checked.
Decision software that needs a notified body is high-risk from 2 August 2028, and Annex III duties start 2 December 2027. Whether this draft is that software is not settled here.
The dossier is kept twenty years after the last change. The filed note sits in that dossier. This design adds no second archive.
A decision based solely on automated processing needs an Article 22 basis. This design does not diagnose or choose the chronic treatment by automation.
Ambient recording can capture staff performance and needs Dutch works-council consent where a council exists. Other countries differ. The draft does not score her.
Model knowledge: showing stored readings and drafting one note are not a measured saving for this employer. The range is a scenario for this visit, not a published percentage.

assumptions: She starts when the patient sits down for this chronic visit and stops when the confirmed note is on the record. She does not run the laboratory. Every step is her time.

The list reads reading type, value and date already stored by the person who entered an earlier clinic or home reading, outside this visit. A blank is omitted. She measures during the exam, which stays at full time. Today's cuff reading is not treated as already stored. Earlier capture is not counted as saved.
The draft uses what she asked, examined and decided in s2 to s4. It does not invent the treatment. A rejected draft is not filed.
Filing is a separate step. It writes only chronic-note-v1, the version she accepted in s7. A later change voids that acceptance and nothing files. The list does not send an out-of-range alert.
Upkeep is 0.5 hour per 100 hours of this task, for a reading on the wrong patient and for a draft that omitted the decision. The check in s7 is already in remaining time and is not deducted again.
unknowns: Whether blood pressure and glucose are stored with type, value and date.
Who enters home readings, and how old a stored reading may be.
Whether a works council exists and whether consultation recording counts as staff monitoring.
research_questions: On a sample of diabetes and blood-pressure visits, how often is a reading already stored before she examines?
How often does she reject the draft?

already_counted.description: Read the draft for a missing diabetes or blood pressure decision.

incremental.description: Correct a reading on the wrong patient, or rewrite a draft that omitted the treatment decision.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a visit where blood pressure or glucose is already stored and she accepts the draft, she skips tallying the old readings and retyping the note. On a blank list, a reading she must take herself, or a rejected draft, the saving is near zero. Asking, examining, deciding and telling the patient are not shortened. The figure is not the published note-time percentage applied to the whole visit.

tasks.short: Prescribe a medication using efficacy, safety and cost, as authorized.

steps.what: List current medications and each priced alternative.
Read efficacy and safety for the medications she may prescribe.
Decide which medications to prescribe on efficacy, safety and cost.
Flag contraindications and duplicates for the medications she chose.
Tell the patient which medications were prescribed and why.
Write the prescription she is legally authorized to sign.

tasks.design: The patient record in {OTHER} lists current medications and priced alternatives only when medication name, indication and price are already stored. After she chooses, a rule check flags contraindications and duplicates for that medication. She still reads efficacy and safety, decides, tells the patient and writes the prescription herself. The check does not prescribe, does not send, and does not alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: Efficacy sat in a document, price sat in a formulary, and the duplicate check was a search she repeated after she had already chosen.
tasks.enabler_now: Stored medication and price can be listed, and a rule check can flag the medication she has named. The choice and the signature stay with her.
tasks.still_hard: Efficacy and safety are a reading and a judgement. A missing price is not a reason to call a medication cheap, and a flag is not a signature.
tasks.human_edge: She weighs efficacy, safety and cost for this patient, and she signs only what she is authorized to prescribe.
tasks.altitude: She still reads, chooses, explains and signs. She stops retyping the current medication list when it is stored, and she stops searching duplicates by hand after she has chosen.

reach.task: Dispenses the medication she signed and may propose a priced substitute.
reach.learn: Which cost line the pharmacist is allowed to substitute.

evidence.claim: The G-Standaard checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates. KNMP sets the content. The check does not choose the medication.
The inspectorate names medication errors that come from a wrong registration and says the provider stays responsible. This design does not let the flag choose the medication.
The cited source is the medicines-law definition of a prescription. This design does not treat a flag or a price list as that prescription. She writes the line herself.
A decision based solely on automated processing needs an Article 22 basis. This design does not choose the medication by automation.

Model knowledge: listing stored medications and prices, and flagging a medication she has already chosen, are not a measured saving for this employer. The range is a scenario for this prescription, not a published percentage.

assumptions: She starts when she is choosing a medication for this patient and stops when she has signed. She does not dispense. Every step is her time.

The list reads current medication name, alternative name, indication and price, stored by the formulary keeper and by earlier prescribers, outside this task. A blank price is omitted. She does not treat a missing price as low cost. The cost judgement stays inside s3 at full time. That earlier capture is not counted as saved.
The efficacy and safety text is a document she reads herself in s2. Nothing drafts that reading.

The flag runs only after she has named the medication in s3. It shows contraindications and duplicates. It does not write the prescription, send it, or alert anyone. A missing current-medication list is shown as missing and does not clear the choice.
She writes and signs in s6. There is no send step because nothing in this design transmits the prescription.
Upkeep is 0.3 hour per 100 hours of this task, for a price or a duplicate row that is stale. Reading flags is inside s5 and s6 and is not deducted again.
unknowns: Whether indication and price are stored as fields, and who maintains them.
Which medications she is legally authorized to prescribe in this country.
Whether the clinic already shows duplicate checks.
research_questions: On a sample of new prescriptions, how often is a price present before she chooses?
How often does a contraindication flag change the medication she signs?

incremental.description: Correct a stale price or a duplicate row before she signs.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a choice where current medications and prices are filled, she skips retyping the list and the hand search for duplicates. On a blank price, a medication she changes after the flags, or a safety text she must read in full, the saving is near zero. Reading efficacy, deciding, telling the patient and signing are not shortened. The figure is not a published prescribing percentage.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Her week is still the exam, the diagnosis, the treatment and the signature. She stops hunting the record when problem, medication, result, age, blood pressure, glucose and price are filled, and she stops retyping a note she has already checked.
reach: physician: which findings to hand over in an emergency
pharmacist: which interaction flag is a hard stop on a dosage
registered nurse: which blood pressure reading to repeat before the next visit
skills_to_grow: Diagnose an unstable condition from the exam, not from the problem list.
Set a dosage from the patient in front of her when a flag is only a warning.
Judge a chronic problem from the visit, not from the glucose list.
Choose a medication on efficacy and safety when the price is blank.
role.ambitious_version: She still examines, diagnoses, treats and signs. A blank result, a blank price and a rejected draft stay off the record. Nothing files a note she has not checked, and nothing prescribes in her place.
